Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/onboarding

Welcome the developer or QA engineer and explain what this skill does in one sentence.
Then proceed through the phases below. Ask one question at a time. Do not front-load.

---

## Phase 1 — Role and context

Ask:
> "Are you joining as a developer or a QA engineer?"

Wait for the answer. Then:

**If developer:** Ask:
> "Which squad are you on — Squad A (checkout, cart, payments, order management, tax, GivX) or Squad B (Homepage, PDP, PLP, search, account, Brochureware Content)?"

**If QA:** No squad question needed — QA covers both squads.

Ask (both roles):
> "Is this your first time working on this project, or are you returning on a new machine?"

New = full walkthrough. Returning on new machine = focus on mechanical setup, skip orientation.

---

## Phase 2 — Mechanical setup checks

Run these checks inline using the Bash tool. Report results as you go.

```bash
node --version
npm --version
claude --version 2>/dev/null || echo "NOT FOUND"
git branch --show-current
ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg' || echo "hooks missing"
```

For each issue found:

**Hooks missing:**
> "The git hooks aren't installed on this machine. Run both of these now:"
```bash
cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
```
Verify after: `ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'`

**On develop or main:**
> "You're on the `{branch}` branch. You must always work on a feature branch. Create one now:"
```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup
```

**Node too old:** Point to the project's node requirement (24 LTS) and ask them to update before continuing.

**Claude Code not found:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`.

Once all checks pass, say: "Setup is confirmed. Let's cover the rules and tools."

---

## Phase 3 — Developer orientation

*Skip this phase for QA — go to Phase 4.*

### Rules overview

Walk through these in order — brief, one at a time, confirm understanding before continuing.

**Branch rule (non-negotiable):**
> "Never work directly on `develop` or `main`. Every task gets a feature branch.
> Before each session: `git branch --show-current`. If it says develop, stop."

**Protection tiers:**
> "Every file in this repo has a tier. Tier 1 = frozen, you cannot touch it without explicit
> owner approval. Tier 2 = protected, requires a second reviewer on the PR.
> The Tier 1 list is in [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md). Read it before your first task."

Point them to the full tier map: [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) and [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md).

**TypeScript-only rule:**
> "Every file you create or modify under `overrides/` must be `.ts` or `.tsx`.
> `.js`/`.jsx` are not acceptable in that folder — including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`."

**Hard Rule #12:**
> "If requirements are unclear, Claude will ask one clarifying question at a time and wait.
> If you're prompting Claude and it asks a question, answer it before sending the next instruction."

**Contact map:**
Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) contact map section. Tell them:
> "Design tokens → UI Designer (#design-system). Commerce hooks → Integration Lead (#integration).
> Checkout / cart → Squad A Lead. PDP / search / account → Squad B Lead."

### Sprint order

Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Tell them which sprint the project is currently in.

> "We're in Sprint [N]. That means [what exists]. Code from Sprint [N+1] doesn't exist yet —
> don't reference it in your tasks."

### Squad-specific orientation

**Squad A (checkout, cart, payments):**
> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/checkout/`, `overrides/app/components/order-summary/`,
> `overrides/app/components/promo-code/`, and `overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/`.
> Before touching the header, footer, or shared product components, message Squad B Lead."

**Squad B (PDP, PLP, search, account):**
> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, `overrides/app/pages/product-list/`,
> `overrides/app/pages/account/`, and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`.
> Before touching checkout or cart components, message Squad A Lead."

### Key skills

Tell them which skills to reach for first:
- [/session-start](../session-start/SKILL.md) — run at the start of every session (mandatory)
- [/feature-spec](../feature-spec/SKILL.md) — before starting any non-trivial implementation
- [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) — before opening a PR
- [/pr-checklist](../pr-checklist/SKILL.md) — to generate PR description
- [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) — when you need E2E test coverage for a user journey

### First task

> "Your first task: read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) and [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) end to end.
> Then run `/session-start` to see the current project state.
> When you have a ticket to work on, start with `/feature-spec` before writing any code."

---

## Phase 4 — QA orientation

*Skip this phase for developers — they went through Phase 3.*

### The QA model

> "This project uses a human-in-the-lead QA model. Claude generates tests — you validate them.
> A test is not complete until you have approved the Gherkin `.feature` file.
> Never accept a Playwright spec without reading and confirming the `.feature` file first."

### Testing layers

Three layers, three purposes (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing):
1. **Vitest** — unit logic.
2. **Storybook `play` functions** — component interactions.
3. **Playwright** — E2E user journeys (this is where Gherkin lives).

### Feature file workflow

Walk through the workflow:
1. Developer creates a Jira story.
2. Developer runs [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) in Claude Code.
3. Claude drafts a Gherkin `.feature` file and **stops**.
4. QA reads the `.feature` file — it's in `e2e/features/{area}/`.
5. QA annotates corrections in the file with `# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]`.
6. Developer runs `/qa-generate` again with the annotation.
7. Claude updates the feature file (confirm), then generates the Playwright spec.

Point them to `e2e/features/README.md` and the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page.

### Tags they must verify

Every `.feature` file needs:
- `@{JIRA-KEY}` — Jira traceability for Zephyr. **If missing, results won't sync.**
- `@{area}` — functional area tag
- `@p0` — only on confirmed critical paths (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant selection)

> "If a feature file is missing the Jira tag, flag it to the developer before the test is generated."

### Magento baseline regression

> "Files in `e2e/features/regression/` document Magento 2 expected behaviour.
> When a baseline test fails against SFCC, do NOT update it to pass.
> Add `# DELTA:` and bring it to the next standup for classification."

### BrowserStack and Zephyr

> "BrowserStack cross-browser runs trigger automatically on PRs to `release/**`.
> Results link to your Zephyr stories via BrowserStack Test Observability.
> Check with the delivery lead that your Jira account has access to the BrowserStack project."

### First task

> "Your first task: read the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page end to end.
> Then review the reference `.feature` file under `e2e/features/checkout/`. If you spot anything that reads like a technical implementation detail rather than plain English, that's exactly the kind of thing to flag in an annotation."

---

## Phase 5 — Confirm and close

Ask:
> "Any questions before you start?"

Answer questions, one at a time. Then close with:
> "You're set up. Run `/session-start` at the start of every session — it reads the tracking
> docs and confirms where the project is before any code is written.
> If something is unclear mid-task, ask in #dev-team before running Claude Code on it."

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- contentful-drift-check: Check for drift between React component props and their Contentful Studio component definitions. Use when a developer wants to verify definitions are still in sync after props have changed, or to audit all registered components at once.
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.

- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.

There's no in-session tool to rename a session that's currently running, though — it's applied at launch/resume time from the terminal.

To apply "mainSession" to this session, run this in a **new terminal tab** (not inside this live session, since renaming the session while it's the active process could conflict with its own transcript write):

```
claude --resume 4f15e6f5-7d1a-490e-968c-40527b35b551 --name mainSession
```

That will resume this exact conversation under the name "mainSession" going forward, and it'll persist — you'll see it in the `/resume` picker from then on.
